text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today to $150.80, its highest close in two weeks, as oil prices spiked on escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude topped $116 a barrel—a six-month high—after Saudi Arabia reported intercepting Iranian-backed Houthi attacks on energy infrastructure, and as the Trump administration signaled potential military action against Iran. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly boost the value of reserves in the ground and improve refining and production margins.

The two-week rally of 12.45% reflects a broader shift in energy markets driven by supply-risk premiums: regional conflict is making investors see U.S. energy assets—oil producers and liquefied natural gas exporters especially—as safer bets in a tightening global market. The gap between world oil ($115.22) and U.S. oil ($107.89) also widens the profit opportunities for companies with international operations.
